skill_drafts.name: Next.js Image Optimization
skill_drafts.description: Optimize images in Next.js applications using the built-in `next/image` component to reduce file size, improve load performance, and enable responsive sizing with automatic format conversion.
applicable_signals: Performance metrics show image payload as bottleneck
Need for responsive image delivery across device sizes
contraindications: Images already optimized externally or via third-party CDN with no Next.js integration required
Static images served directly from public directory without component wrapping
workflow_steps: Import Image component from next/image
Replace standard tags with component
Set src, alt, width, and height props (or use fill layout)
Optionally configure priority, sizes, or quality props
Verify responsive srcset and lazy loading in browser DevTools
triggers: Application contains images requiring responsive sizing
Images need lazy loading to improve initial page load
Format conversion (WebP, AVIF) is desired for performance
constraints: Images must be imported or have explicit dimensions (width/height) or fill layout
next/image component requires Next.js 10.0.0 or later
cautions: Lazy loading is enabled by default; use priority prop only for above-the-fold images to avoid performance regression
Ensure image dimensions are set correctly to prevent layout shift
output_contract: Images are served with automatic format selection, responsive srcset attributes, and lazy loading enabled by default. Caller receives optimized image delivery with reduced payload and improved render performance.

metadata.prompt: Use the `next/image` component to wrap image assets. Configure responsive sizing via width/height props or fill layout. Enable lazy loading (default) and automatic format selection (WebP, AVIF). Verify images are served with appropriate srcset and lazy-loading attributes.

skill_drafts.name: Next.js Font Loading Optimization
skill_drafts.description: Optimize web fonts using the built-in `next/font` loaders to reduce font file size, improve text rendering performance, and eliminate layout shift during font load.
applicable_signals: Custom font files referenced in layout or page components
Multiple font weights or variants required
Performance audit flags font-related CLS or LCP issues
contraindications: System fonts only (no custom fonts needed)
Fonts already optimized via external CDN with proper caching
Font files served from third-party provider with built-in optimization
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify custom or third-party fonts in use', 'detail': 'Audit application for font files and external font sources'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure next/font loader', 'detail': 'Import and configure font loader with appropriate subsetting and weight options'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply font to layout or page component', 'detail': 'Assign loaded font to CSS class or style variable for use in components'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Define fallback font stack', 'detail': 'Ensure fallback fonts match loaded font metrics to minimize layout shift'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify preloading and subset behavior', 'detail': 'Test font loading in browser DevTools; confirm no CLS during font load'}
triggers: Application uses custom or third-party web fonts
Page load time is impacted by font delivery
Font rendering causes visible layout shift
constraints: Font loader configuration must be applied at layout or page level
Subsetting strategy should match actual character usage in application
Fallback font stack must be defined to prevent layout shift
cautions: Ensure font preloading does not conflict with other resource priorities
Test font loading behavior across network conditions (slow 3G, 4G)
Verify no duplicate font requests after optimization
output_contract: Fonts are preloaded and subset automatically; no cumulative layout shift (CLS) occurs during font load; font file size is reduced through subsetting; text renders with optimized font without blocking page interaction.

metadata.prompt: Use the built-in `next/font` loaders to configure and optimize web fonts in your Next.js application. Configure font subsetting, preloading, and fallback strategies to ensure fonts load efficiently without causing cumulative layout shift (CLS).

skill_drafts.name: Third-Party Script Performance Optimization
skill_drafts.description: Optimize third-party scripts (analytics, ads, tracking) using the built-in Script component to control loading strategy and prevent main-thread blocking.
applicable_signals: presence of Google Analytics, ad networks, or tracking pixels
performance metrics show script-related rendering delays
build optimization phase or performance improvement initiative
contraindications: Scripts are critical for initial page render or above-the-fold content
Scripts are already optimized via external loader or CDN strategy
Script execution order is tightly coupled and cannot be deferred
workflow_steps: Identify all third-party scripts in the application
Classify each script by criticality: critical (beforeInteractive), standard (afterInteractive), or deferred (lazyOnload)
Wrap each script with the built-in Script component and assign the appropriate strategy
Test page rendering and script functionality with each strategy
Monitor performance metrics and script execution timing
Adjust strategies based on performance data and functional requirements
triggers: Application integrates external scripts for analytics, ads, or tracking
Performance audit identifies third-party scripts blocking main thread
Need to defer non-critical script execution
constraints: Script component must wrap the external script tag
Loading strategy must match script criticality and use case
Verify script functionality after applying deferred loading
cautions: beforeInteractive strategy blocks page render; use only for truly critical scripts
lazyOnload may delay analytics or tracking data collection; monitor data completeness
Test script behavior across different loading strategies before production deployment
output_contract: Scripts are loaded according to assigned strategy; main thread is unblocked for non-critical scripts; performance metrics (LCP, FID, CLS) show improvement or remain stable; all scripts execute correctly and collect data as expected.

metadata.prompt: Use the built-in Script component to wrap third-party scripts and apply appropriate loading strategies. Choose from beforeInteractive (critical, blocks render), afterInteractive (default, non-blocking), or lazyOnload (deferred until interaction). This prevents scripts from blocking the main thread and improves overall page performance.

skill_drafts.name: JavaScript Bundle Analysis and Reduction
skill_drafts.description: Analyze and reduce JavaScript bundle size using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to identify and eliminate unnecessary code. This workflow helps diagnose performance bottlenecks caused by large bundles and guides removal of unused dependencies.
applicable_signals: large JavaScript payload in network waterfall
contraindications: bundle size is already within acceptable limits
analysis tools are not available or cannot be installed
workflow_steps: Install and configure @next/bundle-analyzer plugin in the Next.js project
Run the analyzer on a production build to generate bundle report
Review the report to identify large or unused dependencies
Evaluate each large dependency for necessity and alternatives
Remove or replace unnecessary packages
Re-run the analyzer to confirm size reduction
Test application functionality after changes
triggers: performance metrics indicate slow initial load
need to diagnose bundle composition before optimization
constraints: requires @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to be installed and configured
analysis should be run on production build output
changes to dependencies must be tested for functionality impact
cautions: removing dependencies without testing may break application features
bundle size reduction must be balanced against feature completeness
output_contract: Bundle analysis report generated; unused or oversized dependencies identified; bundle size reduced and verified through re-analysis

metadata.prompt: Use the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to generate a detailed report of your JavaScript bundle composition. Review the report to identify large or unused dependencies. Remove or replace unnecessary packages, then re-run the analyzer to confirm size reduction.

skill_drafts.name: Application Performance Monitoring with OpenTelemetry
skill_drafts.description: Instrument Next.js applications with OpenTelemetry to collect and export performance metrics, traces, and logs for monitoring and debugging in production environments.
contraindications: No monitoring backend or observability platform available
Instrumentation overhead is unacceptable for the use case
workflow_steps: Install and configure OpenTelemetry SDK and exporters for Next.js
Initialize instrumentation at application startup
Configure trace and metric exporters to target observability backend
Verify telemetry data is being collected and exported
Monitor observability platform to confirm traces and metrics are visible
triggers: Distributed tracing is required for debugging
Performance metrics need to be collected and exported
Observability platform is available and configured
constraints: Observability platform must be configured and accessible
Exporters must be properly initialized before application startup
Telemetry collection should not significantly impact application performance
cautions: Ensure sensitive data is not captured in traces or logs
Monitor instrumentation overhead and adjust sampling rates if needed
Verify exporter connectivity before relying on telemetry data
output_contract: Telemetry data (traces, metrics, logs) successfully exported to monitoring backend; traces and metrics visible and queryable in observability platform; instrumentation active without critical performance degradation.

metadata.prompt: Set up OpenTelemetry instrumentation in your Next.js application to enable distributed tracing, metric collection, and log export. Configure exporters to send telemetry data to your chosen observability backend. Verify that traces and metrics are being captured and transmitted correctly.
